notes: Parts door for Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd. Every statement about the South African company comes from site-za/content-brief/brief.txt; nothing is taken from memory or industry knowledge. Decisions: (1) Parts is one page (brief section 3). Its four anchors are form, categories, aog and verify. The two prose anchors are the sections array, in the fixed order (categories, aog). #form is the form block's own id (form.id is 'form', as on the engines door, so the hero call to action and the nav anchor resolve to it) and #verify is the verify block, which the builder renders with id 'verify', as it renders the aircraft process block at #process. The brief lists the page in the order request form, categories, AOG line, how we verify parts; the builder decides whether the form comes first, and the hero call to action jumps to #form either way. (2) The brief says the profile has sixteen product categories but does not name them, so the categories section explains that every category comes through one page and names no category; there is no fullScope accordion. Both are flagged. (3) No process block: CONTENT-SCHEMA.md assigns the nine-step transaction process to the aircraft door, and the brief gives no parts-specific sequence; flagged, because brief section 4 also mentions the parts page. (4) The verify block carries the five checks the brief names (traceability, release documentation, certification status, incident and accident history, remaining life), each with a plain one-line gloss and no added claim. (5) The release certificate field offers Yes, No and Not sure, because naming certificate types would be industry knowledge and a coverage claim; flagged. (6) The part number field is a textarea so several lines can be pasted (brief section 5: allow several lines); a spreadsheet goes by email because the fixed field list has no upload field; flagged. (7) AOG: the form's aog field is the segmented Yes or No that DoorForm reads; when Yes is chosen and the WhatsApp number exists, the component shows the WhatsApp route with the site.json template. The disclaimer line under the button tells the visitor that. Until the number exists, the AOG section links to the contact page's urgent block, which the component upgrades to the WhatsApp deep link later. (8) No response time, no staffed hours, no region, no airports, no aircraft types, no approvals, no figures, no years: the brief gives none for parts. (9) Currency: parts are quoted in US dollars (brief section 6). (10) No image key: imagery is placed by the build agent and marked as placeholder in the hand-over note. British English, no dashes as punctuation, headlines 8 words or fewer, paragraphs 40 words or fewer, bullets 8 words or fewer.

clientToConfirm: Product categories: the brief says the corporate profile lists sixteen product categories but does not name them, so the categories section names none and there is no 'Full scope' accordion. Supply the list to render it in the categories section and in an accordion for procurement readers.

Release certificates: the form asks only whether a release certificate is needed (Yes, No, Not sure). Supply the certificate types Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd can actually supply, and the select will list them instead.

WhatsApp Business number and staffed hours in SAST for the AOG line: neither exists yet. The AOG section links to the contact page's urgent block, and the form's WhatsApp route appears only once the number is set in site.json. No hours are stated.
Response time for AOG and for standard parts requests: none is stated anywhere on the page. Commit to one, stated in SAST, only if the team can staff it.

Inboxes: parts@flighthoursolution.com is a proposal for the form and for spreadsheet RFQs (it appears in the part number hint). Confirm the address and who it forwards to, and whether AOG requests should also go to aog@ (the form routes to one inbox; the WhatsApp line is the AOG route).
Spreadsheets for RFQs: brief section 5 mentions a spreadsheet upload. The fixed field list has no upload field, so the page asks for the spreadsheet by email. Confirm, or approve adding a file field.
Parts-distribution accreditation and any SACAA-related approval (brief section 1): none is rendered. Supply the real list, with certificate numbers, before any accreditation is named on this page.
Condition options: confirm the four (New, Overhauled, Serviceable, As removed) and whether a buyer who will accept any condition needs a fifth choice.
Currency: the page and the form say parts are quoted in US dollars, as the brief states. Confirm.

Transaction process: brief section 4 asks for the transaction process on the Aircraft and Parts pages; CONTENT-SCHEMA.md assigns the nine-step process to Aircraft, and the brief gives no parts-specific sequence. Confirm whether the profile has one to publish here.

Verification wording: the five checks (traceability, release documentation, certification status, incident and accident history, remaining life) are the brief's list, each with a plain one-line gloss. Confirm the glosses describe what the team actually checks on every parts request.
Stock or sourcing: the page describes sourcing against a part number. Confirm whether Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd also holds its own stock, in which case the categories section can say so.
Regions, delivery airports and aircraft types: none are named. The form asks for the delivery airport and the aircraft type as free text. Confirm the regions and aircraft types to name once decided.
Form choices: approve the AOG label 'Aircraft on ground' with its hint, the part number field accepting several lines, and the description field being optional.

Engine families: the page names Pratt & Whitney, Honeywell, IAE and CFM as the families you take part requests for, from your message. Confirm the list and the order, and whether any other family belongs there. The names appear as plain text only, with no logos.

Quantity on the form: a request from the engine viewer can hold several part numbers, each with its own quantity, written one per line in the part number field; the single Quantity field is filled with the total. Confirm, or say if the Quantity field should become optional.
